intro: A low-dimensional representation saves space by discarding directions. Reconstruct it to see which information survives.
task: Center observations using a supplied mean, project onto supplied orthonormal component rows, and reconstruct in the original feature space.
requirements: X is a nonempty finite (n,d) matrix. mean has shape (d,). components has shape (k,d), with 1 <= k <= d.
Component rows must be orthonormal: components @ components.T equals identity within absolute tolerance 1e-7 and relative tolerance zero.
Return scores (n,k) and reconstruction (n,d) in a dictionary. Use the supplied mean; do not fit a new mean or components.
Do not modify inputs. Raise ValueError for the invalid shapes, ranges, or non-finite numeric inputs described above. Numerical checks use moderate finite values unless stated otherwise.

examples.name: Discard second coordinate
examples.output:
{'scores': [[2], [4]], 'reconstruction': [[3, 2], [5, 2]]}
(Numeric values rounded to 8 decimal places where needed.)

examples.output:

hints.title: Choose the representation
hints.body: The forward multiplication is (X - mean) @ components.T.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: A learned mean is part of a fitted transform. Refitting it on these observations changes the representation.

explanation: Projection takes dot products with basis directions. Orthonormal rows ensure each score measures a coordinate without counting the same direction twice.
Multiplying scores by the components returns to feature space; adding the supplied mean reverses centering. Missing directions cannot be recovered from the scores.
Compare a one-component reconstruction with a complete orthonormal basis. The full basis recovers every input; the smaller basis exposes the discarded residual.
